Key insight: the journal requires `debit > 0` or `credit > 0` strictly. A negative-amount credit note would FAIL the one-side CHECK (negative is neither > 0). So a credit note modeled as a negative-amount `CustomerInvoice` would NOT post cleanly through the existing AR service.

The cleanest approach: model the credit note as a **separate, minimal finance credit-note path** that builds the reversing journal (Dr revenue / Cr AR / Dr output tax) with positive amounts on the flipped sides. This mirrors how `customer_invoices.py` builds its journal but swaps debit↔credit.

4	A delivery records the physical shipment of goods against a CONFIRMED sales order. The header mixes
5	in ``DocumentMixin`` and carries a gapless ``delivery_number`` claimed at creation (D-040). It is
6	built DRAFT (a shipping clerk picks order lines + source bins + quantities) and then POSTED: at POST
7	the stock ISSUE moves are created (Dr COGS / Cr Inventory via the inventory costing event — COGS is
8	the DEFAULT ISSUE offset, no override), the order lines' delivered_quantity rises, the order
9	advances PARTIALLY_DELIVERED/DELIVERED — all one transaction.
10	
11	``sales_order_id`` is a composite tenant FK to sales_orders (the delivery is always against an
12	order in v1). ``customer_id`` is a SNAPSHOT of the order's customer (so reporting reads the customer
13	without re-resolving the order — the GR vendor-snapshot precedent). ``warehouse_id`` is an OPAQUE
14	inventory warehouse id (validated via inventory/queries, never a cross-module FK — D-029); each
15	line's ``bin_id`` is likewise an opaque inventory bin id (where the stock is issued FROM).
16	
17	Per D-041 the delivery↔stock-move linkage is recorded via DOCFLOW (delivery document → 'moved_by' →
18	move document), NOT a cross-module ``stock_move_id`` FK column — inventory owns the move, so a
19	delivery line does not carry a foreign key into another module's table (the goods-receipt
20	precedent).
21	"""
22	
23	import uuid
24	from datetime import date, datetime
25	
26	import sqlalchemy as sa
27	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
28	
29	from app.core.docflow import DocumentMixin, document_fk
30	from app.core.models import (
31	    AuditMixin,
32	    Base,
33	    TenantMixin,
34	    TimestampMixin,
35	    UuidPKMixin,
36	    tenant_fk,
37	    tenant_unique,
38	)
39	from app.core.money import QuantityType
40	from app.modules.sales.constants import DeliveryStatus
41	
42	
43	class Delivery(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, DocumentMixin, Base):
44	    """An outbound-delivery header (PLAN 7.3). ``delivery_number`` is claimed at creation (D-040).
45	    ``sales_order_id`` is a composite tenant FK to sales_orders; ``customer_id`` is a snapshot of
46	    the order's customer; ``warehouse_id`` is an OPAQUE inventory warehouse id (validated via
47	    inventory/queries — D-029). ``status`` runs the DeliveryStatus lifecycle (DRAFT → POSTED; DRAFT
48	    → CANCELLED). ``shipping_address`` (nullable) is a free-text ship-to snapshot; ``posted_at``
49	    records when the shipment committed. Audited (D-010)."""
50	
51	    __tablename__ = "sales_deliveries"
52	    __table_args__ = (
53	        tenant_unique(),
54	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
55	        document_fk(),
56	        tenant_fk("sales_orders", "sales_order_id"),
57	        # PERFORMANCE §1: the delivery list filters on (tenant, status) and an order's deliveries.
58	        sa.Index("ix_sales_deliveries_tenant_id_status", "tenant_id", "status"),
59	        sa.Index(
60	            "ix_sales_deliveries_tenant_id_sales_order_id",
61	            "tenant_id",
62	            "sales_order_id",
63	        ),
64	    )
65	
66	    delivery_number: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=False)
67	    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
68	        sa.String(20),
69	        nullable=False,
70	        default=DeliveryStatus.DRAFT.value,
71	        server_default="DRAFT",
72	    )
73	    sales_order_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
74	    # Customer snapshot from the order at create (reporting reads it without re-resolving the
75	    # order).
76	    customer_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
77	    # Opaque inventory warehouse id (D-029) the shipment's stock issues FROM; each line's bin is in
78	    # it.
79	    warehouse_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
80	    delivery_date: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=False)
81	    shipping_address: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(1000), nullable=True)
82	    notes: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(1000), nullable=True)
83	    posted_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(
84	        sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True
85	    )
86	
87	
88	class DeliveryLine(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
89	    """One shipped item on a delivery (PLAN 7.3). ``sales_order_line_id`` is a composite tenant FK
90	    to sales_order_lines (the line being delivered against). ``item_id`` is an OPAQUE inventory item
91	    id snapshot from the order line; ``bin_id`` is an OPAQUE inventory bin id (where the stock is
92	    issued FROM — D-029, validated via inventory/queries). ``quantity`` is the shipped quantity on
93	    this line (≤ the order line's open-to-deliver). ``lot_code`` / ``serial_code`` (nullable) are
94	    passed to the stock move for lot/serial-tracked items. UNIQUE(tenant_id, delivery_id,
95	    line_number). NOT AuditMixin (header-line exclusion). No stock_move_id column — the
96	    delivery↔move link is docflow (D-041)."""
97	
98	    __tablename__ = "sales_delivery_lines"
99	    __table_args__ = (
100	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
101	            "tenant_id", "delivery_id", "line_number", name="uq_sales_delivery_lines_delivery_line"
102	        ),
103	        tenant_unique(),
104	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
105	        tenant_fk("sales_deliveries", "delivery_id"),
106	        tenant_fk("sales_order_lines", "sales_order_line_id"),
107	    )
108	
109	    delivery_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
110	    line_number: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=False)
111	    sales_order_line_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
112	    item_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
113	    bin_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
114	    quantity: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(QuantityType(), nullable=False)
115	    lot_code: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(100), nullable=True)
116	    serial_code: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(100), nullable=True)

content.content:
1	"""Sales constants (STRUCTURE §3): the customer-master + pricing enums, the pricing-engine defaults,
2	and the permission keys, registered into the core RBAC catalog at import (D-009).
3	
4	A SINGLE file (STRUCTURE §8.4: split into a constants/ package only at the 400-line cap, the
5	finance precedent); PLAN 7.1's customer master + condition-style pricing and PLAN 7.2's quote →
6	order document chain sit under that. The delivery/invoice document chain (7.3–7.4) will add its own
7	status enums, document types and number sequences here as it lands.
8	
9	**Customer codes are USER-SUPPLIED and unique per tenant** (the ``UNIQUE(tenant_id, customer_code)``
10	on sales_customers) — mirroring the procurement ``vendor_code`` and inventory ``item_code``: a
11	customer MASTER carries no gapless document number (a code, not a number). The SALES DOCUMENTS in
12	7.2+ (quotes, orders, deliveries, invoices) DO claim gapless numbers — a posted document in the
13	D-012 sense — but the master does not.
14	
15	**Credit-limit semantics (decided here, D-043).** ``Customer.credit_limit`` is a non-null
16	``MoneyType`` defaulting to 0 and meaning the maximum outstanding AR (open invoices) the customer
17	may carry. It is interpreted as:
18	
19	- ``0`` (the default) → CASH-ONLY: the customer is allowed no open credit at all, so 7.2's order
20	  confirmation blocks if confirming would leave ANY positive outstanding AR. New customers are
21	  cash-only until a limit is set explicitly.
22	- a positive value → the credit ceiling: 7.2 blocks confirmation when outstanding AR + the new
23	  order would exceed it.
24	
25	There is deliberately NO "unlimited" sentinel in v1 (a NULL credit_limit is NOT used): "unlimited"
26	is expressed by setting a very large explicit limit, keeping the column non-null and the 7.2 check a
27	single unconditional comparison with no NULL branch. This is the static credit-limit block the
28	s4hana-parity Sales section scopes to v1 (no exposure aggregation across open orders/deliveries, no
29	finance-owned exposure ledger — documented there as a later).
30	
31	**Customer group (decided here).** A customer optionally belongs to ONE ``CustomerGroup`` — a lean
32	``sales_customer_groups`` (tenant, code, name) MASTER table, NOT a free-string column. A master
33	table is chosen because pricing keys on the group: a ``PriceList`` targets a group by id (a
34	composite tenant FK), so both the customer and the price list reference the same group rows, the
35	group's name is editable in one place, and a typo'd free-string group can never silently exclude a
36	customer from its price list. The group carries NO pricing of its own — it is purely a grouping key.
37	"""
38	
39	from enum import StrEnum
40	
41	from app.core.rbac import register_permissions
42	
43	
44	class CustomerStatus(StrEnum):
45	    """A customer's lifecycle / usability state (parity: customer master block levels).
46	
47	    - ACTIVE: usable — new quotes/orders may name this customer (the only state 7.2+ accepts).
48	    - BLOCKED: temporarily barred — kept for history and existing open documents, but the O2C chain
49	      (7.2) refuses to confirm a NEW order against it (a soft block, distinct from the credit-limit
50	      block; the customer can be unblocked back to ACTIVE).
51	    - INACTIVE: retired — no new business, retained for reporting and existing AR history.
52	
53	    Transitions are unrestricted between the three (ACTIVE↔BLOCKED↔INACTIVE all allowed): a block is
54	    reversible and a retired customer can be reactivated. The only rule the service enforces is that
55	    the target is a valid CustomerStatus; no terminal state, because customer history must stay
56	    referenceable and a mistaken retire/block must be undoable (the append-only ledger lives in
57	    finance AR, not here) — the procurement VendorStatus precedent."""
58	
59	    ACTIVE = "ACTIVE"
60	    BLOCKED = "BLOCKED"
61	    INACTIVE = "INACTIVE"
62	
63	
64	class PriceListStatus(StrEnum):
65	    """A price list's usability state. Only ACTIVE lists are considered by the price resolver; an
66	    INACTIVE list is retained (history, a seasonal list parked between campaigns) but never priced
67	    from. Transitions are unrestricted between the two (a list can be re-activated)."""
68	
69	    ACTIVE = "ACTIVE"
70	    INACTIVE = "INACTIVE"
71	
72	
73	class QuoteStatus(StrEnum):
74	    """Lifecycle of a sales quotation — the pre-sales document (PLAN 7.2).
75	
76	    All transitions are set IN 7.2 (a quote is a wholly-sales document; no later phase touches it):
77	
78	    - DRAFT: created, editable; lines can change. The QUO number is claimed AT CREATION (D-012/D-040
79	      claim-at-creation — a quote is referenceable the moment it exists, the procurement-document
80	      precedent, not finance's number-at-post).
81	    - SENT: issued to the customer (DRAFT→SENT). Lines are frozen.
82	    - ACCEPTED: the customer accepted (SENT→ACCEPTED) — the only state convertible to an order.
83	    - REJECTED: the customer declined (SENT→REJECTED); terminal.
84	    - EXPIRED: ``valid_until`` has passed without acceptance — a lazy state the service sets on
85	      access/sweep (DRAFT/SENT → EXPIRED); terminal-ish (a fresh quote is raised instead).
86	    - CONVERTED: an order was raised from an ACCEPTED quote (the order's ``source_quote_id`` is
87	    set);
88	      terminal — a converted quote is not re-converted or edited.
89	    - CANCELLED: abandoned before conversion (from DRAFT/SENT/ACCEPTED); terminal."""
90	
91	    DRAFT = "DRAFT"
92	    SENT = "SENT"
93	    ACCEPTED = "ACCEPTED"
94	    REJECTED = "REJECTED"
95	    EXPIRED = "EXPIRED"
96	    CONVERTED = "CONVERTED"
97	    CANCELLED = "CANCELLED"
98	
99	
100	class SalesOrderStatus(StrEnum):
101	    """Lifecycle of a sales order — the committing O2C document (PLAN 7.2). CONFIRMED is the key
102	    gate this phase implements; the later O2C phases drive the fulfilment/billing states.
103	
104	    States SET in 7.2:
105	
106	    - DRAFT: created (from scratch or from an ACCEPTED quote), editable; the SO number is claimed AT
107	      CREATION (D-012/D-040). The customer is validated ACTIVE at create.
108	    - CONFIRMED: the confirm gate passed (ATP evaluated + credit within limit). A CONFIRMED order is
109	      a firm commitment whose undelivered quantity COMMITS stock against ATP for subsequent orders
110	      (D-044). This is the state 7.3 deliveries pick from.
111	    - CREDIT_BLOCKED: confirmation was attempted but the credit exposure (open AR + open confirmed
112	      orders + this order) exceeded the customer's credit_limit — the HARD block (D-044). A user
113	      with
114	      ``sales.order.credit_release`` releases it (credit_check_status RELEASED) and re-confirms.
115	    - CANCELLED: abandoned before any delivery/invoice; terminal (a delivered/invoiced order is
116	      corrected downstream, never cancelled).
117	
118	    States driven by LATER phases (declared now as the full lifecycle, transitions land later):
119	
120	    - PARTIALLY_DELIVERED / DELIVERED: set by 7.3 outbound deliveries as ``delivered_quantity``
121	    rises
122	      on the lines (DELIVERED when every line is fully delivered).
123	    - INVOICED: set by 7.4 billing once the order is fully invoiced.
124	    - CLOSED: fully delivered + invoiced (or short-closed); terminal."""
125	
126	    DRAFT = "DRAFT"
127	    CONFIRMED = "CONFIRMED"
128	    CREDIT_BLOCKED = "CREDIT_BLOCKED"
129	    PARTIALLY_DELIVERED = "PARTIALLY_DELIVERED"
130	    DELIVERED = "DELIVERED"
131	    INVOICED = "INVOICED"
132	    CLOSED = "CLOSED"
133	    CANCELLED = "CANCELLED"
134	
135	
136	class DeliveryStatus(StrEnum):
137	    """Lifecycle of an outbound delivery — the O2C fulfilment document (PLAN 7.3), the outbound twin
138	    of the procurement goods receipt (the GoodsReceiptStatus precedent, mirrored).
139	
140	    - DRAFT: created, editable; a shipping clerk picks order lines + source bins + quantities. The
141	      DN number is claimed AT CREATION (D-012/D-040 claim-at-creation — a delivery is referenceable
142	      the moment it exists, the goods-receipt precedent). No stock has moved yet.
143	    - POSTED: the delivery shipped (DRAFT → POSTED). At POST it ISSUES stock (one inventory ISSUE
144	      move per line, via the event bus) — each move's costing posts Dr COGS / Cr Inventory — raises
145	      the order lines' delivered_quantity, and advances the order (PARTIALLY_DELIVERED / DELIVERED).
146	      All ONE transaction (D-011/D-020). TERMINAL: a POSTED delivery has moved stock + posted COGS,
147	      so it is corrected by a return / RMA (7.4), never cancelled or re-posted — the goods-receipt
148	      terminal-POSTED precedent.
149	    - CANCELLED: a DRAFT delivery abandoned before posting (DRAFT → CANCELLED); moves nothing."""
150	
151	    DRAFT = "DRAFT"
152	    POSTED = "POSTED"
153	    CANCELLED = "CANCELLED"
154	
155	
156	class CreditCheckStatus(StrEnum):
157	    """The result of an order's confirm-time credit check (PLAN 7.2, D-044), stored on the order so
158	    the UI + audit can see why a confirmation blocked and that it was released.
159	
160	    - PASSED: exposure (open AR + open confirmed orders + this order) was within the credit limit;
161	      the order confirmed normally.
162	    - BLOCKED: exposure exceeded the limit at confirmation — the order is CREDIT_BLOCKED and not
163	      confirmed (the HARD block per parity).
164	    - RELEASED: a user with ``sales.order.credit_release`` overrode the block; the order may then
165	      confirm (the release is recorded, the audit trail carries who/when via the audit row)."""
166	
167	    PASSED = "PASSED"
168	    BLOCKED = "BLOCKED"
169	    RELEASED = "RELEASED"
170	
171	
172	class DiscountType(StrEnum):
173	    """How a per-order-LINE discount is expressed (PLAN 7.2 applies it; defined here so the wire
174	    contract is stable from the start, the MatchStatus-declared-early precedent).
175	
176	    - PERCENT: a percentage off the resolved base price (e.g. 10 = 10% off).
177	    - AMOUNT: an absolute amount off per unit in the line's currency.
178	
179	    The PRICE LIST itself carries no discount — it yields the base unit price only (the condition
180	    base). Discounts are an order-line concern (7.2), so the resolver in 7.1 returns the base price
181	    untouched; this enum is the vocabulary those lines will use."""
182	
183	    PERCENT = "PERCENT"
184	    AMOUNT = "AMOUNT"
185	
186	
187	# The default net-days a customer is created with when the payload omits it (NET30 — the common
188	# commercial default; AR's due-date math is invoice_date + this many days). Stored on the customer
189	# with a CHECK >= 0; mirrors the procurement vendor payment-terms model.
190	DEFAULT_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS = 30
191	
192	# A customer's credit_limit defaults to 0 = CASH-ONLY (D-043, documented in the module docstring):
193	# no open credit allowed. Stored on the customer as a non-null MoneyType with a CHECK >= 0.
194	DEFAULT_CREDIT_LIMIT = 0
195	
196	# A new price list's default priority. When several ACTIVE lists match the same item/customer/date/
197	# currency/quantity, the resolver picks the HIGHEST priority first (D-043 resolution order); equal
198	# priorities fall through to specificity (group-targeted beats general) then latest valid_from. A
199	# higher integer = higher priority. The default 0 means "no explicit priority"; a tenant raises a
200	# list's priority to make it win ties. Stored with a CHECK >= 0.
201	DEFAULT_PRICE_LIST_PRIORITY = 0
202	
203	
204	# --- Permissions (D-009): one key per guarded endpoint action -----------------
205	# Customer master (PLAN 7.1): read the customer master (+ customer groups) vs create/edit it.
206	# Customer-group management rides CUSTOMER_MANAGE (the inventory item/uom-conversion precedent:
207	# closely-related master config shares the parent entity's manage key — a group is a customer
208	# grouping, managed by whoever manages customers).
209	SALES_CUSTOMER_READ = "sales.customer.read"
210	SALES_CUSTOMER_MANAGE = "sales.customer.manage"
211	# Price lists (PLAN 7.1): read the price lists (+ their items, + a resolved price quote) vs
212	# create/edit them (and their items). Pricing is a distinct authority from the customer master.
213	SALES_PRICELIST_READ = "sales.pricelist.read"
214	SALES_PRICELIST_MANAGE = "sales.pricelist.manage"
215	
216	# Quotes (PLAN 7.2): read the quote register vs create/edit/send/accept/reject/convert. A quote
217	# carries no committing gate (sending/accepting a quote moves no money or stock), so MANAGE covers
218	# every quote action — the RFQ-manage precedent (sourcing is not a committing action).
219	SALES_QUOTE_READ = "sales.quote.read"
220	SALES_QUOTE_MANAGE = "sales.quote.manage"
221	# Sales orders (PLAN 7.2): read vs create/edit/convert/cancel vs the privileged CONFIRM action vs
222	# the privileged CREDIT_RELEASE action.
223	#   - CONFIRM is its own key (the journal.post / po.approve precedent): confirming runs the ATP
224	#     evaluation + the credit-limit gate, a distinct authority from drafting an order.
225	#   - CREDIT_RELEASE is its own key (an approval-like override): releasing a CREDIT_BLOCKED order
226	#     past the limit is a manager's call, recorded in the audit trail. A clerk who can confirm
227	#     cannot silently override a credit block.
228	SALES_ORDER_READ = "sales.order.read"
229	SALES_ORDER_MANAGE = "sales.order.manage"
230	SALES_ORDER_CONFIRM = "sales.order.confirm"
231	SALES_ORDER_CREDIT_RELEASE = "sales.order.credit_release"
232	
233	# Deliveries (PLAN 7.3): read the delivery register vs create/edit/cancel the DRAFT vs the
234	# privileged POST action (issue stock + post the COGS journal). POST is its own key (the
235	# journal.post / goods_receipt.post precedent): building a delivery note and shipping it — which
236	# moves stock and posts COGS — are separate authorities. A clerk who picks a delivery cannot
237	# silently post the goods issue.
238	SALES_DELIVERY_READ = "sales.delivery.read"
239	SALES_DELIVERY_MANAGE = "sales.delivery.manage"
240	SALES_DELIVERY_POST = "sales.delivery.post"
241	
242	register_permissions(
243	    SALES_CUSTOMER_READ,
244	    SALES_CUSTOMER_MANAGE,
245	    SALES_PRICELIST_READ,
246	    SALES_PRICELIST_MANAGE,
247	    SALES_QUOTE_READ,
248	    SALES_QUOTE_MANAGE,
249	    SALES_ORDER_READ,
250	    SALES_ORDER_MANAGE,
251	    SALES_ORDER_CONFIRM,
252	    SALES_ORDER_CREDIT_RELEASE,
253	    SALES_DELIVERY_READ,
254	    SALES_DELIVERY_MANAGE,
255	    SALES_DELIVERY_POST,
256	    descriptions={
257	        SALES_CUSTOMER_READ: "Read customers and customer groups",
258	        SALES_CUSTOMER_MANAGE: "Create and edit customers and customer groups",
259	        SALES_PRICELIST_READ: "Read price lists, their items and resolved price quotes",
260	        SALES_PRICELIST_MANAGE: "Create and edit price lists and their items",
261	        SALES_QUOTE_READ: "Read sales quotations",
262	        SALES_QUOTE_MANAGE: "Create, edit, send, accept, reject and convert sales quotations",
263	        SALES_ORDER_READ: "Read sales orders",
264	        SALES_ORDER_MANAGE: "Create, edit, convert and cancel sales orders",
265	        SALES_ORDER_CONFIRM: "Confirm sales orders (run the ATP and credit-limit checks)",
266	        SALES_ORDER_CREDIT_RELEASE: "Release a credit-blocked sales order past the credit limit",
267	        SALES_DELIVERY_READ: "Read outbound deliveries",
268	        SALES_DELIVERY_MANAGE: "Create, edit and cancel draft deliveries",
269	        SALES_DELIVERY_POST: "Post deliveries (issue stock and post the COGS journal)",
270	    },
271	)
272	
273	
274	# --- Document types + number sequences (D-012/D-040) --------------------------
275	# The two O2C documents register in core_documents and claim a gapless number AT CREATION (D-040:
276	# claim-at-creation so a quote/order is referenceable the moment it exists — the
277	# procurement-document
278	# precedent, not finance's number-at-post branch). Sequences year-reset (QUO-2026-00001 /
279	# SO-2026-00001). Gaplessness still holds because creation is the committing transaction.
280	QUOTE_DOC_TYPE = "sales.quote"
281	QUOTE_SEQUENCE_NAME = "sales.quote"
282	QUOTE_NUMBER_PREFIX = "QUO"
283	QUOTE_NUMBER_PADDING = 5
284	
285	SALES_ORDER_DOC_TYPE = "sales.order"
286	SALES_ORDER_SEQUENCE_NAME = "sales.order"
287	SALES_ORDER_NUMBER_PREFIX = "SO"
288	SALES_ORDER_NUMBER_PADDING = 5
289	
290	# docflow link type joining the chain (D-012 vocabulary). The edge is predecessor → successor, so
291	# the
292	# link_type names the edge from the predecessor's point of view: an ACCEPTED quote is "converted_to"
293	# the order raised from it (the order carries source_quote_id; the quote→order edge is the chain the
294	# DocFlowViewer renders). The reverse ("quoted_by") is the successor's view, kept here for the docs.
295	QUOTE_CONVERTED_TO_ORDER_LINK = "converted_to"
296	
297	# Delivery (PLAN 7.3): the outbound fulfilment document. Registers in core_documents + claims a
298	# gapless DN number AT CREATION (D-040; year-resetting DN-2026-00001), the goods-receipt precedent.
299	# A delivery is built DRAFT then POSTED; the POST issues stock (an inventory ISSUE move per line)
300	# whose costing posts COGS — but the delivery claims its OWN DN- number, distinct from the STK- the
301	# inventory move claims.
302	DELIVERY_DOC_TYPE = "sales.delivery"
303	DELIVERY_SEQUENCE_NAME = "sales.delivery"
304	DELIVERY_NUMBER_PREFIX = "DN"
305	DELIVERY_NUMBER_PADDING = 5
306	
307	# Delivery docflow edges (PLAN 7.3, D-041). The edge is predecessor → successor named from the
308	# predecessor's point of view:
309	#   order → delivery   : the sales order is "delivered_by" the delivery (written by sales at POST).
310	#   delivery → move    : the delivery is "moved_by" each inventory ISSUE move it generates (written
311	#                        by INVENTORY's handler when it creates the moves — the GR "moved_by"
312	#                        precedent; the delivery↔move linkage is docflow, NOT a cross-module FK).
313	ORDER_DELIVERED_BY_DELIVERY_LINK = "delivered_by"
314	DELIVERY_MOVED_BY_STOCK_MOVE_LINK = "moved_by"
315	
316	# The sales domain event the delivery POST publishes (D-011/D-041): inventory's handlers.py
317	# subscribes and creates the stock ISSUE moves in the SAME transaction (the sanctioned cross-module
318	# mechanism — sales never imports inventory/service). Mirrors GOODS_RECEIPT_POSTED_EVENT_KEY, but
319	# the event carries NO GL accounts: an ISSUE move's default offset IS the item-category COGS
320	# account (resolved inside the costing engine), so unlike the GR/IR receipt there is no offset to
321	# override.
322	DELIVERY_SHIPPED_EVENT_KEY = "sales.delivery.shipped"

1	"""Domain events sales PUBLISHES (D-011/D-041). Declarative data only — no logic, no models — so
2	inventory's ``handlers.py`` may import these typed classes (the STRUCTURE §5 events.py allowance:
3	an event carries no behaviour, so a subscriber in another module imports it without any logic).
4	
5	``DeliveryShipped`` is the SANCTIONED cross-module mechanism for the delivery → stock-issue effect
6	(D-045), the OUTBOUND TWIN of procurement's ``GoodsReceiptPosted`` (D-041, mirrored). Sales OWNS the
7	delivery document and its sales order; it MUST NOT call inventory's service directly (STRUCTURE §5
8	forbids importing another module's service). So the delivery POST publishes this event carrying
9	everything inventory needs to create the stock ISSUE moves — one ``DeliveryMove`` per delivery line
10	(item, the SOURCE bin to issue from, quantity, lot/serial) plus the move_date and the delivery's
11	core_documents id for docflow linkage. Inventory's ``handlers.py`` subscribes, creates each move via
12	its OWN service with ``move_type=ISSUE``, and links delivery document → 'moved_by' → move document.
13	The handler shares the session, so the moves + their COGS/inventory journals land in the SAME
14	transaction as the delivery post — all-or-nothing (D-011/D-020): a closed period or any handler
15	failure (e.g. insufficient stock) rolls the WHOLE delivery post back.
16	
17	The KEY DIFFERENCE from ``GoodsReceiptPosted`` (D-045): the event carries NO GL accounts. A receipt
18	overrode its valuation offset to the GR/IR clearing account (a three-way-match leg), so that event
19	carried ``gr_ir_account_id``. An ISSUE move's DEFAULT valuation offset IS the item category's COGS
20	account (resolved inside the costing engine from the item's category), so a delivery needs no offset
21	override — COGS *is* the issue offset — and the event carries no account at all.
22	
23	Sales updates its OWN tables (the order-line delivered_quantity, the order status, the delivery
24	status/posted_at) in that same transaction AFTER publishing; it does NOT need the move ids back —
25	the delivery↔move link is the durable docflow edge the handler writes, not a cross-module FK column
26	(D-041/D-045).
27	"""
28	
29	import uuid
30	from decimal import Decimal
31	from typing import ClassVar
32	
33	from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
34	
35	from app.core.events import DomainEvent
36	from app.modules.sales.constants import DELIVERY_SHIPPED_EVENT_KEY
37	
38	
39	class DeliveryMove(BaseModel):
40	    """One delivery line's worth of stock to issue (D-045), the payload inventory's handler turns
41	    into a stock ISSUE move. Plain frozen data: the opaque item + SOURCE bin ids (D-029), the
42	    quantity issued in the item's base UoM, and optional lot/serial IDS (the lot/serial the stock
43	    leaves on for tracked items). The ids are RESOLVED by sales at create time from the line's
44	    lot/serial codes — an ISSUE references an EXISTING lot/serial by id (unlike a receipt, it
45	    creates none). No unit cost — the costing engine COMPUTES the COGS of the stock that left (FIFO
46	    layers / moving-average), unlike a receipt which enters at a supplied cost."""
47	
48	    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
49	
50	    item_id: uuid.UUID
51	    bin_id: uuid.UUID
52	    quantity: Decimal
53	    lot_id: uuid.UUID | None = None
54	    serial_id: uuid.UUID | None = None
55	
56	
57	class DeliveryShipped(DomainEvent):
58	    """A delivery was posted / shipped (D-045). Inventory's ``handlers.py`` subscribes and creates
59	    one stock ISSUE move per ``move`` in the SAME transaction, each offsetting to the item-category
60	    COGS account by DEFAULT (Dr COGS / Cr Inventory — no offset override, unlike the GR/IR receipt),
61	    and links the delivery document to each move document ('moved_by').
62	
63	    - ``delivery_id`` + ``delivery_number`` + ``document_id`` — the delivery document
64	      (``document_id`` is the core_documents id the handler links the move documents to).
65	    - ``warehouse_id`` — the inventory warehouse the shipment's stock issues from (each move's bin
66	      is in it); carried for context / future per-warehouse routing.
67	    - ``move_date`` — the delivery date the stock moves post on (ISO date string); a date in a
68	      CLOSED period makes each move's COGS journal trip the period trigger, rolling the delivery
69	      back.
70	    - ``moves`` — the per-line issues (see ``DeliveryMove``)."""
71	
72	    key: ClassVar[str] = DELIVERY_SHIPPED_EVENT_KEY
73	
74	    delivery_id: uuid.UUID
75	    delivery_number: str
76	    document_id: uuid.UUID
77	    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID
78	    move_date: str
79	    moves: tuple[DeliveryMove, ...]
80	
81	
82	__all__ = ["DeliveryMove", "DeliveryShipped"]
83

1	"""Sales' cross-module read interface (STRUCTURE §5).
2	
3	Sales sits above inventory and finance in the dependency order: the O2C documents in 7.2–7.4
4	(quote → order → delivery → invoice) and finance AR reporting read THIS file to resolve customer
5	state + prices synchronously; sales imports finance/queries + inventory/queries downward. Keep this
6	surface thin and stable — it is a contract; it is the ONLY sales file other modules import.
7	
8	The central D-029 link: finance AR stores a customer on each invoice/receipt as an opaque
9	``partner_id`` (no FK). ``get_customer_for_partner`` resolves that ``partner_id`` back to a
10	``Customer`` so AR aging / reporting can render the customer's name and payment terms — the
11	``partner_id`` IS the ``Customer.id``, so it is a thin alias over ``get_customer`` named for the
12	reporting intent (the exact mirror of procurement's ``get_vendor_for_partner``).
13	
14	The PRICE RESOLVER is exposed here too: ``resolve_price`` is the public entry point 7.2's order
15	entry prices each line through, delegating to ``service/price_resolution.resolve_price`` (the
16	deterministic best-match picker, D-043). Putting it in queries.py keeps the rule that other modules
17	import only this file.
18	
19	PLAN 7.2 adds the ORDER reads 7.3 (deliveries) + 7.4 (billing) call — ``get_sales_order``,
20	``so_line_open_to_deliver`` (ordered − delivered), ``get_order_for_delivery`` — and the ATP + credit
21	helpers the confirm gate + order UI use: ``committed_quantity`` (the reservation = confirmed-
22	undelivered demand per item), ``atp_check`` (availability = on-hand − committed + on-order, D-044),
23	``open_confirmed_order_value`` + ``customer_open_ar`` (the credit-exposure components).
24	``atp_check`` + ``customer_open_ar`` make SANCTIONED downward cross-module reads (inventory
25	on-hand, procurement on-order, finance open AR) — sales is above all three (STRUCTURE §5).
26	
27	Every function takes an explicit ``tenant_id`` and runs under the caller's tenant context, so the
28	D-007 filter applies on top of the explicit predicate — ordinary tenant-scoped reads, not a bypass.
29	"""
30	
31	import uuid
32	from dataclasses import dataclass
33	from datetime import date
34	from decimal import Decimal
35	
36	from sqlalchemy import select
37	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
38	
39	from app.modules.finance import queries as finance_queries
40	from app.modules.inventory import queries as inventory_queries
41	from app.modules.procurement import queries as procurement_queries
42	from app.modules.sales.constants import CustomerStatus, SalesOrderStatus
43	from app.modules.sales.models import Customer, SalesOrder, SalesOrderLine
44	from app.modules.sales.service.price_resolution import ResolvedPrice
45	from app.modules.sales.service.price_resolution import resolve_price as _resolve_price
46	
47	
48	async def get_customer(
49	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, customer_id: uuid.UUID
50	) -> Customer | None:
51	    """The customer with ``customer_id`` in the tenant, or None. Lets another module read a
52	    customer's master fields (name, status, default currency, payment terms, credit limit) without
53	    importing sales models directly — the analogue of procurement's ``get_vendor``."""
54	    stmt = select(Customer).where(
55	        Customer.tenant_id == tenant_id, Customer.id == customer_id
56	    )
57	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
58	
59	
60	async def get_customer_for_partner(
61	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, partner_id: uuid.UUID
62	) -> Customer | None:
63	    """The customer an AR document's opaque ``partner_id`` refers to (D-029), or None. AR aging /
64	    reporting calls this to resolve an invoice's ``partner_id`` to a customer name + payment terms.
65	    The ``partner_id`` IS the ``Customer.id`` (finance stores it without an FK), so this is
66	    ``get_customer`` named for the reporting intent — kept as its own function so AR call sites read
67	    intent-first and the alias survives any future indirection (the vendor precedent)."""
68	    return await get_customer(session, tenant_id, partner_id)
69	
70	
71	async def customer_exists(
72	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, customer_id: uuid.UUID
73	) -> bool:
74	    """Whether a customer with ``customer_id`` exists in the tenant. The cheap existence check a
75	    quote / order line uses to validate its customer_id (the sales analogue of inventory's
76	    ``item_exists``)."""
77	    stmt = select(Customer.id).where(
78	        Customer.tenant_id == tenant_id, Customer.id == customer_id
79	    )
80	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).first() is not None
81	
82	
83	async def customer_status(
84	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, customer_id: uuid.UUID
85	) -> CustomerStatus | None:
86	    """The customer's lifecycle status (ACTIVE/BLOCKED/INACTIVE), or None if the customer does not
87	    exist. 7.2's order flow reads this to refuse a NEW order against a non-ACTIVE customer (the soft
88	    block, distinct from the credit-limit block)."""
89	    stmt = select(Customer.status).where(
90	        Customer.tenant_id == tenant_id, Customer.id == customer_id
91	    )
92	    value = (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
93	    return CustomerStatus(value) if value is not None else None
94	
95	
96	async def customer_credit_limit(
97	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, customer_id: uuid.UUID
98	) -> Decimal | None:
99	    """The customer's static credit limit = max outstanding AR (D-043), or None if the customer does
100	    not exist. 7.2's order confirmation reads this for the credit-limit block: 0 = cash-only (no
101	    open credit allowed), a positive value = the ceiling. Exposed so the order flow need not import
102	    sales models."""
103	    stmt = select(Customer.credit_limit).where(
104	        Customer.tenant_id == tenant_id, Customer.id == customer_id
105	    )
106	    value = (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
107	    return Decimal(str(value)) if value is not None else None
108	
109	
110	async def customer_payment_terms_days(
111	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, customer_id: uuid.UUID
112	) -> int | None:
113	    """The customer's net-days payment terms (e.g. 30 = NET30), or None if the customer does not
114	    exist. The order→invoice flow (7.4) reads this to default an invoice's due date (invoice_date +
115	    days), the same math AR uses today — exposed so the chain need not import sales models."""
116	    stmt = select(Customer.payment_terms_days).where(
117	        Customer.tenant_id == tenant_id, Customer.id == customer_id
118	    )
119	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
120	
121	
122	async def customer_default_currency(
123	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, customer_id: uuid.UUID
124	) -> str | None:
125	    """The customer's default currency code (ISO alpha-3), or None if the customer does not exist.
126	    The quote/order flow (7.2) defaults a document's currency from this; exposed so the chain need
127	    not import sales models."""
128	    stmt = select(Customer.default_currency_code).where(
129	        Customer.tenant_id == tenant_id, Customer.id == customer_id
130	    )
131	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
132	
133	
134	async def resolve_price(
135	    session: AsyncSession,
136	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
137	    *,
138	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
139	    customer_id: uuid.UUID,
140	    on_date: date,
141	    quantity: Decimal,
142	    currency: str,
143	) -> ResolvedPrice:
144	    """The applicable base unit price for an item/customer/date/quantity/currency (PLAN 7.1, D-043).
145	
146	    The public entry point 7.2's order entry prices each line through. Delegates to the
147	    deterministic best-match resolver in ``service/price_resolution`` (documented there); returns a
148	    :class:`ResolvedPrice` whose ``matched`` is False when no ACTIVE price list applies. Bounded to
149	    two queries — no N+1. Exposed here so other modules import only ``sales/queries``."""
150	    return await _resolve_price(
151	        session,
152	        tenant_id,
153	        item_id=item_id,
154	        customer_id=customer_id,
155	        on_date=on_date,
156	        quantity=quantity,
157	        currency=currency,
158	    )
159	
160	
161	# --- Sales-order reads (PLAN 7.2 → consumed by 7.3 deliveries + 7.4 billing) ------------------
162	
163	
164	async def get_sales_order(
165	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_id: uuid.UUID
166	) -> SalesOrder | None:
167	    """The sales order with ``order_id`` in the tenant, or None. Lets 7.3 (deliveries) and 7.4
168	    (billing) read an order header — customer, currency, status, totals — without importing sales
169	    service internals. A point lookup on the PK."""
170	    stmt = select(SalesOrder).where(
171	        SalesOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id, SalesOrder.id == order_id
172	    )
173	    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()
174	
175	
176	async def so_line_open_to_deliver(
177	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_line_id: uuid.UUID
178	) -> Decimal | None:
179	    """The still-open-to-deliver quantity on an order line — ORDERED minus DELIVERED — or None if
180	    the line does not exist (PLAN 7.2 → 7.3). A delivery (7.3) caps a pick at this. A point lookup
181	    on the maintained ``delivered_quantity`` (raised by 7.3), not a SUM over deliveries."""
182	    line = (
183	        await session.execute(
184	            select(SalesOrderLine).where(
185	                SalesOrderLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
186	                SalesOrderLine.id == order_line_id,
187	            )
188	        )
189	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
190	    if line is None:
191	        return None
192	    return Decimal(str(line.ordered_quantity)) - Decimal(str(line.delivered_quantity))
193	
194	
195	async def get_order_for_delivery(
196	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_id: uuid.UUID
197	) -> tuple[SalesOrder, list[SalesOrderLine]] | None:
198	    """The order header + its lines (item, ordered/delivered quantities, unit price, tax code) — the
199	    data a delivery (7.3) needs to build pick lines and billing (7.4) needs to invoice. None when
200	    the order is unknown to this tenant. Two indexed reads (header by PK, lines by (tenant,
201	    order_id)); no N+1 over lines."""
202	    order = await get_sales_order(session, tenant_id, order_id)
203	    if order is None:
204	        return None
205	    lines = list(
206	        (
207	            await session.execute(
208	                select(SalesOrderLine)
209	                .where(
210	                    SalesOrderLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
211	                    SalesOrderLine.order_id == order_id,
212	                )
213	                .order_by(SalesOrderLine.line_number)
214	            )
215	        )
216	        .scalars()
217	        .all()
218	    )
219	    return order, lines
220	
221	
222	async def so_line_open_to_invoice(
223	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_line_id: uuid.UUID
224	) -> Decimal | None:
225	    """The still-open-to-invoice quantity on an order line — DELIVERED minus INVOICED — or None if
226	    the line does not exist (PLAN 7.3 → 7.4). 7.4 bills against DELIVERED-but-not-yet-INVOICED
227	    quantity (you invoice what shipped, not what was ordered), so this caps an invoice line at
228	    delivered − invoiced, NOT ordered − invoiced. A point lookup on the maintained columns."""
229	    line = (
230	        await session.execute(
231	            select(SalesOrderLine).where(
232	                SalesOrderLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
233	                SalesOrderLine.id == order_line_id,
234	            )
235	        )
236	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
237	    if line is None:
238	        return None
239	    return Decimal(str(line.delivered_quantity)) - Decimal(str(line.invoiced_quantity))
240	
241	
242	async def get_order_for_invoice(
243	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_id: uuid.UUID
244	) -> tuple[SalesOrder, list[SalesOrderLine]] | None:
245	    """The order header + its lines for BILLING (PLAN 7.3 → 7.4): the data 7.4's invoice run needs
246	    to bill the DELIVERED-but-not-yet-invoiced quantity (delivered − invoiced per line). None when
247	    the order is unknown to this tenant. The same two-read shape as ``get_order_for_delivery``
248	    (header by PK, lines by (tenant, order_id)), named for the billing intent; no N+1 over lines."""
249	    return await get_order_for_delivery(session, tenant_id, order_id)
250	
251	
252	# --- ATP: committed quantity + the availability check (PLAN 7.2, D-044) -----------------------
253	
254	
255	async def committed_quantity(
256	    session: AsyncSession,
257	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
258	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
259	    *,
260	    exclude_order_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
261	) -> Decimal:
262	    """The quantity of an item COMMITTED by confirmed-but-undelivered sales orders (PLAN 7.2, D-044)
263	    — the reservation an ATP scan subtracts from on-hand. Sums ``ordered − delivered`` over order
264	    lines for ``item_id`` on CONFIRMED / PARTIALLY_DELIVERED orders (a CONFIRMED order has reserved
265	    its undelivered quantity; a DRAFT / CREDIT_BLOCKED / CANCELLED / fully-DELIVERED / INVOICED /
266	    CLOSED order commits nothing). ``exclude_order_id`` drops one order from the sum — used when
267	    confirming so an order's own demand is checked against availability NET of other commitments.
268	
269	    SET-BASED (no per-order N+1, PERFORMANCE §2): one join over order lines filtered by the order's
270	    status + a positive open quantity, summed in PYTHON over the (small) open set so the
271	    exact-decimal QuantityType round-trips identically on both engines (D-015: SQL never subtracts
272	    two scaled quantity columns for the result value)."""
273	    stmt = (
274	        select(SalesOrderLine.ordered_quantity, SalesOrderLine.delivered_quantity)
275	        .join(
276	            SalesOrder,
277	            (SalesOrderLine.tenant_id == SalesOrder.tenant_id)
278	            & (SalesOrderLine.order_id == SalesOrder.id),
279	        )
280	        .where(
281	            SalesOrderLine.tenant_id == tenant_id,
282	            SalesOrderLine.item_id == item_id,
283	            SalesOrder.status.in_(
284	                [
285	                    SalesOrderStatus.CONFIRMED.value,
286	                    SalesOrderStatus.PARTIALLY_DELIVERED.value,
287	                ]
288	            ),
289	            SalesOrderLine.delivered_quantity < SalesOrderLine.ordered_quantity,
290	        )
291	    )
292	    if exclude_order_id is not None:
293	        stmt = stmt.where(SalesOrder.id != exclude_order_id)
294	    rows = (await session.execute(stmt)).all()
295	    return sum(
296	        (Decimal(str(ordered)) - Decimal(str(delivered)) for ordered, delivered in rows),
297	        Decimal(0),
298	    )
299	
300	
301	@dataclass(frozen=True)
302	class AtpResult:
303	    """The ATP outcome for one item (D-044): ``available`` = on_hand − committed + on_order;
304	    ``atp_ok`` is ``available >= requested``; ``shortfall`` is ``requested − available`` clamped at
305	    0. Informational — a shortfall flags a backorder, it does NOT block confirmation."""
306	
307	    item_id: uuid.UUID
308	    requested_quantity: Decimal
309	    on_hand: Decimal
310	    committed: Decimal
311	    on_order: Decimal
312	    available: Decimal
313	    atp_ok: bool
314	    shortfall: Decimal
315	
316	
317	async def atp_check(
318	    session: AsyncSession,
319	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
320	    *,
321	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
322	    quantity: Decimal,
323	    on_date: date,
324	    exclude_order_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
325	) -> AtpResult:
326	    """Available-to-promise for one item (PLAN 7.2, D-044): availability = inventory on-hand
327	    (``total_on_hand``) − committed (confirmed-undelivered sales orders) + on-order (procurement
328	    ``open_incoming_quantity``). ``on_date`` is accepted for the wire contract (v1 availability is
329	    a point-in-time snapshot — date-phased ATP is the documented later). Three bounded cross-module
330	    reads (inventory on-hand, sales committed, procurement on-order); no N+1. ``exclude_order_id``
331	    excludes one order from the committed sum (confirm checks an order net of OTHER commitments)."""
332	    requested = Decimal(str(quantity))
333	    on_hand = Decimal(str(await inventory_queries.total_on_hand(session, tenant_id, item_id)))
334	    committed = await committed_quantity(
335	        session, tenant_id, item_id, exclude_order_id=exclude_order_id
336	    )
337	    on_order = Decimal(
338	        str(await procurement_queries.open_incoming_quantity(session, tenant_id, item_id))
339	    )
340	    available = on_hand - committed + on_order
341	    shortfall = requested - available
342	    if shortfall < 0:
343	        shortfall = Decimal(0)
344	    return AtpResult(
345	        item_id=item_id,
346	        requested_quantity=requested,
347	        on_hand=on_hand,
348	        committed=committed,
349	        on_order=on_order,
350	        available=available,
351	        atp_ok=available >= requested,
352	        shortfall=shortfall,
353	    )
354	
355	
356	# --- Credit exposure (PLAN 7.2, D-044) --------------------------------------------------------
357	
358	
359	async def open_confirmed_order_value(
360	    session: AsyncSession,
361	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
362	    customer_id: uuid.UUID,
363	    *,
364	    exclude_order_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
365	) -> Decimal:
366	    """The total value of a customer's OPEN confirmed orders not yet billed (PLAN 7.2, D-044) — the
367	    open-order side of credit exposure. Sums ``total_amount`` over the customer's CONFIRMED /
368	    PARTIALLY_DELIVERED / DELIVERED orders (committed but not yet fully invoiced; an INVOICED
369	    order's exposure has moved to AR, a CLOSED/CANCELLED/DRAFT/CREDIT_BLOCKED order is nothing).
370	    ``exclude_order_id`` drops one order (the one being confirmed, counted separately).
371	
372	    SET-BASED (no per-order N+1): one filtered scan on the (tenant, customer_id, status) index,
373	    summed in Python so the exact-decimal MoneyType round-trips identically on both engines
374	    (D-015)."""
375	    stmt = select(SalesOrder.total_amount).where(
376	        SalesOrder.tenant_id == tenant_id,
377	        SalesOrder.customer_id == customer_id,
378	        SalesOrder.status.in_(
379	            [
380	                SalesOrderStatus.CONFIRMED.value,
381	                SalesOrderStatus.PARTIALLY_DELIVERED.value,
382	                SalesOrderStatus.DELIVERED.value,
383	            ]
384	        ),
385	    )
386	    if exclude_order_id is not None:
387	        stmt = stmt.where(SalesOrder.id != exclude_order_id)
388	    rows = (await session.execute(stmt)).all()
389	    return sum((Decimal(str(value)) for (value,) in rows), Decimal(0))
390	
391	
392	async def customer_open_ar(
393	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, customer_id: uuid.UUID
394	) -> Decimal:
395	    """The customer's open AR (sum of open_amount on POSTED customer invoices) — the receivables
396	    side of credit exposure (PLAN 7.2, D-044). A thin alias over finance's ``customer_open_balance``
397	    keyed by the opaque partner_id (= Customer.id, D-029), named for the credit-check intent so the

1	"""Outbound-delivery POST (PLAN 7.3, D-045) — the heart — split from ``deliveries.py`` at the
2	400-line cap (STRUCTURE §8.4, the goods_receipts / invoice_match_post precedent). The DRAFT create +
3	its validation helpers + ``cancel_delivery`` stay in ``deliveries.py``; the post path + the
4	post-only tracking/status helpers live here. ``__init__`` re-exports both halves as one ``service``
5	surface (``service.post_delivery`` unchanged).
6	
7	``post_delivery`` is the heart: in ONE transaction it PUBLISHES ``DeliveryShipped`` — inventory's
8	handler creates the stock ISSUE moves (Dr COGS / Cr Inventory via the costing event) — raises each
9	order line's delivered_quantity, advances the order status (PARTIALLY_DELIVERED / DELIVERED), links
10	docflow order→delivery, and sets the delivery POSTED. A closed delivery period trips a move's
11	journal trigger and rolls the WHOLE post back; insufficient stock at a bin rolls it ALL back.
12	
13	Why NO valuation-offset override (vs 6.3's GR/IR override): an ISSUE move's DEFAULT offset is the
14	item-category COGS account (the costing engine routes an ISSUE to COGS), so a delivery posts Dr COGS
15	/ Cr Inventory with no account on the event — COGS *is* the issue offset (D-045/D-020).
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	import uuid
21	from datetime import datetime
22	from decimal import Decimal
23	
24	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
25	
26	from app.core import docflow
27	from app.core.events import publish
28	from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, ValidationFailedError
29	from app.modules.inventory import queries as inventory_queries
30	from app.modules.sales.constants import (
31	    ORDER_DELIVERED_BY_DELIVERY_LINK,
32	    DeliveryStatus,
33	    SalesOrderStatus,
34	)
35	from app.modules.sales.events import DeliveryMove, DeliveryShipped
36	from app.modules.sales.models import Delivery, DeliveryLine, SalesOrder
37	from app.modules.sales.service.delivery_reads import get_delivery, get_delivery_lines
38	from app.modules.sales.service.orders import get_sales_order, get_sales_order_lines
39	
40	
41	async def post_delivery(
42	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, delivery_id: uuid.UUID
43	) -> Delivery:
44	    """Post a DRAFT delivery (PLAN 7.3, D-045) — the heart. In ONE transaction: PUBLISH
45	    ``DeliveryShipped`` so inventory's handler creates the stock ISSUE moves (Dr COGS / Cr
46	    Inventory, COGS being the default ISSUE offset — no override) and finance posts the journals;
47	    raise each order line's delivered_quantity; advance the order status (PARTIALLY_DELIVERED /
48	    DELIVERED); link docflow order→delivery; set the delivery POSTED — all here, before commit
49	    (D-011). A closed delivery period trips a move's COGS-journal trigger and rolls it ALL back;
50	    insufficient stock at a bin rolls it ALL back.
51	
52	    Idempotent re-post is rejected (a POSTED delivery is terminal — corrected by a return / RMA,
53	    7.4). The caller commits via uow; the published event is drained in that same uow."""
54	    delivery = await get_delivery(session, tenant_id, delivery_id)
55	    status = DeliveryStatus(delivery.status)
56	    if status == DeliveryStatus.POSTED:
57	        raise ConflictError(
58	            message="The delivery is already posted",
59	            code="sales.delivery_already_posted",
60	            details={"delivery_id": str(delivery_id)},
61	        )
62	    if status != DeliveryStatus.DRAFT:
63	        raise ConflictError(
64	            message=f"A {delivery.status} delivery cannot be posted",
65	            code="sales.delivery_not_postable",
66	            details={"delivery_id": str(delivery_id), "status": delivery.status},
67	        )
68	
69	    lines = await get_delivery_lines(session, tenant_id, delivery_id)
70	    order_lines = {
71	        line.id: line
72	        for line in await get_sales_order_lines(session, tenant_id, delivery.sales_order_id)
73	    }
74	
75	    moves: list[DeliveryMove] = []
76	    for line in lines:
77	        order_line = order_lines[line.sales_order_line_id]
78	        order_line.delivered_quantity = Decimal(str(order_line.delivered_quantity)) + Decimal(
79	            str(line.quantity)
80	        )
81	        # An ISSUE references an EXISTING lot/serial BY ID (it creates none), so resolve the line's
82	        # human lot/serial code to the inventory id through inventory/queries (D-029) — the move
83	        # would otherwise reject a code on an outbound issue. A tracked line with no resolvable
84	        # lot/serial fails loud here, rolling the post back.
85	        lot_id, serial_id = await _resolve_tracking_ids(session, tenant_id, line)
86	        moves.append(
87	            DeliveryMove(
88	                item_id=line.item_id,
89	                bin_id=line.bin_id,
90	                quantity=Decimal(str(line.quantity)),
91	                lot_id=lot_id,
92	                serial_id=serial_id,
93	            )
94	        )
95	
96	    await _advance_order_status(
97	        session, tenant_id, delivery.sales_order_id, order_lines.values()
98	    )
99	
100	    delivery.status = DeliveryStatus.POSTED.value
101	    delivery.posted_at = datetime.now()
102	    await session.flush()
103	    await docflow.set_document_status(
104	        session, tenant_id, delivery.document_id, status=DeliveryStatus.POSTED.value
105	    )
106	    # Link order document → delivery document ('delivered_by') for the docflow chain (the delivery→
107	    # move edges are written by inventory's handler when it creates the moves — D-045).
108	    order = await session.get(SalesOrder, delivery.sales_order_id)
109	    if order is not None:
110	        await docflow.link_documents(
111	            session,
112	            tenant_id,
113	            predecessor=order.document_id,
114	            successor=delivery.document_id,
115	            link_type=ORDER_DELIVERED_BY_DELIVERY_LINK,
116	        )
117	
118	    # Publish AFTER sales' own writes settle: inventory's handler creates the ISSUE moves (COGS the
119	    # default offset) and finance posts the COGS journals, all drained in this same uow
120	    # (D-011/D-045).
121	    publish(
122	        session,
123	        DeliveryShipped(
124	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
125	            delivery_id=delivery.id,
126	            delivery_number=delivery.delivery_number,
127	            document_id=delivery.document_id,
128	            warehouse_id=delivery.warehouse_id,
129	            move_date=delivery.delivery_date.isoformat(),
130	            moves=tuple(moves),
131	        ),
132	    )
133	    return delivery
134	
135	
136	async def _resolve_tracking_ids(
137	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, line: DeliveryLine
138	) -> tuple[uuid.UUID | None, uuid.UUID | None]:
139	    """Resolve a delivery line's lot/serial CODE to the inventory id an ISSUE move needs (D-045). An
140	    outbound issue references an existing lot/serial by id (it never creates one), so the code is
141	    looked up via inventory/queries; a supplied code that does not resolve fails loud (422) so the
142	    delivery does not post against a non-existent lot/serial. Untracked lines carry no codes ⇒
143	    (None, None) and the move's tracking validator accepts an item with no lot/serial."""
144	    lot_id: uuid.UUID | None = None
145	    serial_id: uuid.UUID | None = None
146	    if line.lot_code is not None:
147	        lot_id = await inventory_queries.lot_id_for_code(
148	            session, tenant_id, line.item_id, line.lot_code
149	        )
150	        if lot_id is None:
151	            raise ValidationFailedError(
152	                message="The referenced lot does not exist for this item",
153	                code="sales.delivery_lot_not_found",
154	                details={"item_id": str(line.item_id), "lot_code": line.lot_code},
155	            )
156	    if line.serial_code is not None:
157	        serial_id = await inventory_queries.serial_id_for_code(
158	            session, tenant_id, line.item_id, line.serial_code
159	        )
160	        if serial_id is None:
161	            raise ValidationFailedError(
162	                message="The referenced serial does not exist for this item",
163	                code="sales.delivery_serial_not_found",
164	                details={"item_id": str(line.item_id), "serial_code": line.serial_code},
165	            )
166	    return lot_id, serial_id
167	
168	
169	async def _advance_order_status(
170	    session: AsyncSession,
171	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
172	    order_id: uuid.UUID,
173	    order_lines,
174	) -> None:
175	    """Advance the order status after a delivery raised the lines' delivered_quantity (PLAN 7.3):
176	    DELIVERED when every line is fully delivered (delivered >= ordered), else PARTIALLY_DELIVERED.
177	    The order + lines are already loaded/mutated in this session, so this reads the in-memory
178	    state."""
179	    fully_delivered = all(
180	        Decimal(str(line.delivered_quantity)) >= Decimal(str(line.ordered_quantity))
181	        for line in order_lines
182	    )
183	    order = await get_sales_order(session, tenant_id, order_id)
184	    new_status = (
185	        SalesOrderStatus.DELIVERED if fully_delivered else SalesOrderStatus.PARTIALLY_DELIVERED
186	    )
187	    order.status = new_status.value
188	    await session.flush()
189	    await docflow.set_document_status(
190	        session, tenant_id, order.document_id, status=new_status.value
191	    )

1	"""Outbound-delivery create / cancel (PLAN 7.3, D-045): create a DRAFT against a sales order, cancel
2	a DRAFT. The POST path (the heart) + its post-only helpers live in ``delivery_post.py`` and the
3	reads in ``delivery_reads.py`` (split at the 400-line cap, STRUCTURE §8.4); the package ``__init__``
4	re-exports all three halves as one ``service`` surface.
5	
6	A delivery records the physical shipment of order goods — the OUTBOUND TWIN of the procurement goods
7	receipt (service/goods_receipts.py, mirrored). ``create_delivery`` writes a DRAFT (validates the
8	order is deliverable, each line belongs to it, the shipped quantity is within the open-to-deliver
9	quantity, the bin checks out and the source bin holds enough stock) and claims the DN number at
10	creation (D-040). No stock moves yet — that is POST (``delivery_post.post_delivery``).
11	
12	Cross-module rule (STRUCTURE §5 / D-045): sales NEVER calls inventory's service — the stock effect
13	goes through the event bus. Sales reads bins / on-hand via inventory/queries (downward reads),
14	updates its OWN order/delivery rows, and lets inventory's handler own the ISSUE moves.
15	"""
16	
17	from __future__ import annotations
18	
19	import uuid
20	from dataclasses import dataclass
21	from datetime import date
22	from decimal import Decimal
23	
24	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
25	
26	from app.core import docflow
27	from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, ValidationFailedError
28	from app.modules.inventory import queries as inventory_queries
29	from app.modules.sales.constants import (
30	    DELIVERY_DOC_TYPE,
31	    DELIVERY_NUMBER_PADDING,
32	    DELIVERY_NUMBER_PREFIX,
33	    DELIVERY_SEQUENCE_NAME,
34	    DeliveryStatus,
35	    SalesOrderStatus,
36	)
37	from app.modules.sales.models import Delivery, DeliveryLine, SalesOrder, SalesOrderLine
38	from app.modules.sales.schemas import DeliveryCreate
39	from app.modules.sales.service._shared import claim_document_number
40	from app.modules.sales.service.delivery_reads import get_delivery
41	from app.modules.sales.service.orders import get_sales_order_lines
42	
43	# A sales order is deliverable once CONFIRMED, or while partially delivered (a follow-up delivery
44	# completes a backorder). DRAFT / CREDIT_BLOCKED / CANCELLED / fully-DELIVERED / INVOICED / CLOSED
45	# cannot start a NEW delivery (D-044: only a firm commitment with open undelivered lines ships).
46	_DELIVERABLE_ORDER_STATUSES = frozenset(
47	    {
48	        SalesOrderStatus.CONFIRMED,
49	        SalesOrderStatus.PARTIALLY_DELIVERED,
50	    }
51	)
52	
53	
54	@dataclass(frozen=True)
55	class _DeliveryLineInput:
56	    """One validated delivery line: the order line it ships against, the snapshot item from that
57	    line, the SOURCE bin, the shipped quantity, and optional lot/serial."""
58	
59	    sales_order_line_id: uuid.UUID
60	    item_id: uuid.UUID
61	    bin_id: uuid.UUID
62	    quantity: Decimal
63	    lot_code: str | None
64	    serial_code: str | None
65	
66	
67	async def _require_deliverable_order(
68	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_id: uuid.UUID
69	) -> SalesOrder:
70	    order = await session.get(SalesOrder, order_id)
71	    if order is None or order.tenant_id != tenant_id:
72	        raise ValidationFailedError(
73	            message="Referenced sales order does not exist",
74	            code="sales.order_not_found",
75	            details={"sales_order_id": str(order_id)},
76	        )
77	    if SalesOrderStatus(order.status) not in _DELIVERABLE_ORDER_STATUSES:
78	        raise ValidationFailedError(
79	            message=f"A {order.status} sales order cannot ship a delivery",
80	            code="sales.order_not_confirmed",
81	            details={"sales_order_id": str(order_id), "status": order.status},
82	        )
83	    return order
84	
85	
86	async def _validate_delivery_line(
87	    session: AsyncSession,
88	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
89	    order_id: uuid.UUID,
90	    order_lines: dict[uuid.UUID, SalesOrderLine],
91	    payload_line: object,
92	) -> _DeliveryLineInput:
93	    """Validate one delivery line against its order line: the line belongs to the order, the qty is
94	    > 0 and within the still-open-to-deliver quantity (over-delivery REJECTED 422 in v1), the
95	    source bin exists in inventory (D-029), and that bin holds enough stock to issue (a clear
96	    pre-check; the move's InsufficientStock guard is the backstop at post). Snapshots the item from
97	    the order line."""
98	    order_line = order_lines.get(payload_line.sales_order_line_id)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
99	    if order_line is None:
100	        raise ValidationFailedError(
101	            message="The delivery line does not belong to this sales order",
102	            code="sales.delivery_line_not_on_order",
103	            details={
104	                "sales_order_id": str(order_id),
105	                "sales_order_line_id": str(
106	                    payload_line.sales_order_line_id  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
107	                ),
108	            },
109	        )
110	    qty = _validate_quantity(payload_line.quantity)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
111	    open_qty = Decimal(str(order_line.ordered_quantity)) - Decimal(
112	        str(order_line.delivered_quantity)
113	    )
114	    if qty > open_qty:
115	        raise ValidationFailedError(
116	            message="The shipped quantity exceeds the order line's open-to-deliver quantity",
117	            code="sales.over_delivery",
118	            details={
119	                "sales_order_line_id": str(order_line.id),
120	                "open_quantity": str(open_qty),
121	                "quantity": str(qty),
122	            },
123	        )
124	    bin_id = payload_line.bin_id  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
125	    if not await inventory_queries.bin_exists(session, tenant_id, bin_id):
126	        raise ValidationFailedError(
127	            message="The source bin does not exist in inventory",
128	            code="sales.delivery_bin_not_found",
129	            details={"bin_id": str(bin_id)},
130	        )
131	    available = await inventory_queries.on_hand(
132	        session, tenant_id, order_line.item_id, bin_id=bin_id
133	    )
134	    if Decimal(str(available)) < qty:
135	        raise ValidationFailedError(
136	            message="The source bin does not hold enough stock to ship this quantity",
137	            code="sales.insufficient_stock",
138	            details={
139	                "bin_id": str(bin_id),
140	                "item_id": str(order_line.item_id),
141	                "on_hand": str(available),
142	                "quantity": str(qty),
143	            },
144	        )
145	    return _DeliveryLineInput(
146	        sales_order_line_id=order_line.id,
147	        item_id=order_line.item_id,
148	        bin_id=bin_id,
149	        quantity=qty,
150	        lot_code=payload_line.lot_code,  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
151	        serial_code=payload_line.serial_code,  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
152	    )
153	
154	
155	def _validate_quantity(quantity: Decimal) -> Decimal:
156	    qty = Decimal(str(quantity))
157	    if qty <= 0:
158	        raise ValidationFailedError(
159	            message="A delivery line quantity must be greater than zero",
160	            code="sales.line_quantity_invalid",
161	            details={"quantity": str(qty)},
162	        )
163	    return qty
164	
165	
166	async def create_delivery(
167	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: DeliveryCreate
168	) -> Delivery:
169	    """Create a DRAFT delivery against a sales order (PLAN 7.3). Validates the order is deliverable
170	    (CONFIRMED / PARTIALLY_DELIVERED → else 422 sales.order_not_confirmed), each line belongs to it,
171	    the quantity is within the open-to-deliver quantity (over-delivery → 422 sales.over_delivery),
172	    the source bin exists, and that bin holds enough stock (422 sales.insufficient_stock). Snapshots
173	    the customer from the order + per-line item from the order line and claims the DN number at
174	    creation (D-040). No stock moves yet — that is POST."""
175	    if not payload.lines:
176	        raise ValidationFailedError(
177	            message="A delivery needs at least one line",
178	            code="sales.delivery_no_lines",
179	        )
180	    order = await _require_deliverable_order(session, tenant_id, payload.sales_order_id)
181	    order_lines = {
182	        line.id: line for line in await get_sales_order_lines(session, tenant_id, order.id)
183	    }
184	    delivery_date = payload.delivery_date or date.today()
185	
186	    validated = [
187	        await _validate_delivery_line(session, tenant_id, order.id, order_lines, line)
188	        for line in payload.lines
189	    ]
190	
191	    delivery_id = uuid.uuid4()
192	    document = await docflow.register_document(
193	        session,
194	        tenant_id,
195	        DELIVERY_DOC_TYPE,
196	        delivery_id,
197	        doc_number=None,
198	        status=DeliveryStatus.DRAFT.value,
199	    )
200	    number = await claim_document_number(
201	        session,
202	        tenant_id,
203	        sequence_name=DELIVERY_SEQUENCE_NAME,
204	        prefix=DELIVERY_NUMBER_PREFIX,
205	        padding=DELIVERY_NUMBER_PADDING,
206	        on_date=delivery_date,
207	    )
208	
209	    delivery = Delivery(
210	        id=delivery_id,
211	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
212	        document_id=document.id,
213	        delivery_number=number,
214	        status=DeliveryStatus.DRAFT.value,
215	        sales_order_id=order.id,
216	        customer_id=order.customer_id,
217	        warehouse_id=payload.warehouse_id,
218	        delivery_date=delivery_date,
219	        shipping_address=payload.shipping_address,
220	        notes=payload.notes,
221	    )
222	    session.add(delivery)
223	    for index, line in enumerate(validated, start=1):
224	        session.add(
225	            DeliveryLine(
226	                tenant_id=tenant_id,
227	                delivery_id=delivery_id,
228	                line_number=index,
229	                sales_order_line_id=line.sales_order_line_id,
230	                item_id=line.item_id,
231	                bin_id=line.bin_id,
232	                quantity=line.quantity,
233	                lot_code=line.lot_code,
234	                serial_code=line.serial_code,
235	            )
236	        )
237	    await session.flush()
238	    await docflow.set_document_status(
239	        session, tenant_id, document.id, doc_number=number, status=DeliveryStatus.DRAFT.value
240	    )
241	    return delivery
242	
243	
244	async def cancel_delivery(
245	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, delivery_id: uuid.UUID
246	) -> Delivery:
247	    """Cancel a DRAFT delivery (PLAN 7.3). A POSTED delivery is TERMINAL — it has issued stock and
248	    posted COGS, so it is corrected by a return / RMA (7.4), never cancelled (v1 has no reverse-
249	    delivery; documented). Cancelling a DRAFT moves nothing."""
250	    delivery = await get_delivery(session, tenant_id, delivery_id)
251	    if DeliveryStatus(delivery.status) != DeliveryStatus.DRAFT:
252	        raise ConflictError(
253	            message=f"A {delivery.status} delivery cannot be cancelled",
254	            code="sales.delivery_not_cancellable",
255	            details={"delivery_id": str(delivery_id), "status": delivery.status},
256	        )
257	    delivery.status = DeliveryStatus.CANCELLED.value
258	    await session.flush()
259	    await docflow.set_document_status(
260	        session, tenant_id, delivery.document_id, status=DeliveryStatus.CANCELLED.value
261	    )
262	    return delivery

59	    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
60	) -> Page[Delivery]:
61	    """Keyset-paginated delivery list, newest first (D-014). The order / status / date filters fold
62	    into the cursor fingerprint; the (tenant, status) and (tenant, sales_order_id) indexes serve the
63	    filtered page (PERFORMANCE §1)."""
64	    stmt = select(Delivery).where(Delivery.tenant_id == tenant_id)
65	    if sales_order_id is not None:
66	        stmt = stmt.where(Delivery.sales_order_id == sales_order_id)
67	    if status is not None:
68	        stmt = stmt.where(Delivery.status == DeliveryStatus(status).value)
69	    if date_from is not None:
70	        stmt = stmt.where(Delivery.delivery_date >= date_from)
71	    if date_to is not None:
72	        stmt = stmt.where(Delivery.delivery_date <= date_to)
73	    return await paginate(
74	        session,
75	        stmt,
76	        order_by=[OrderKey(Delivery.created_at, SortDirection.DESC)],
77	        pk=Delivery.id,
78	        cursor=cursor,
79	        limit=limit,
80	        filters=filter_fingerprint(sales_order_id, status, date_from, date_to),
81	    )
82	
83	
84	async def deliveries_for_order(
85	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, order_id: uuid.UUID
86	) -> list[Delivery]:
87	    """Every delivery raised against a sales order (PLAN 7.3), newest first — the per-order delivery
88	    history the order detail / the 7.4 invoice read. Index-served by (tenant, sales_order_id)."""
89	    stmt = (
90	        select(Delivery)
91	        .where(Delivery.tenant_id == tenant_id, Delivery.sales_order_id == order_id)
92	        .order_by(Delivery.created_at.desc())
93	    )
94	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())
95

1	"""Outbound-delivery HTTP layer (PLAN 7.3), included into the sales router.
2	
3	A sibling router under the same ``/api/v1/sales`` prefix, mounted by ``router.include_router`` in
4	router.py (the order_router precedent — ONE module surface, no second mount in main.py).
5	
6	RBAC (D-009; distinct authorities):
7	  - read by ``sales.delivery.read``;
8	  - create/cancel the DRAFT by ``sales.delivery.manage``;
9	  - the POST action (issue stock + post the COGS journal) by the distinct ``sales.delivery.post``
10	    (the journal.post / goods_receipt.post precedent — building a delivery note and shipping it are
11	    separate rights).
12	
13	Writes commit through ``run_in_uow`` (D-011) so the delivery + its N stock ISSUE moves + N COGS
14	journals + the order update commit (or roll back) atomically; the document-creating + post endpoints
15	are IDEMPOTENT (D-013). The list is O(1) queries + paginated (PERFORMANCE §6).
16	"""
17	
18	import uuid
19	
20	from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
21	
22	from app.core.deps import CurrentUserDep, SessionDep
23	from app.core.events import run_in_uow
24	from app.core.idempotency import Idempotent, IdempotentDep
25	from app.core.pagination import CursorParams, cursor_params, map_page
26	from app.core.rbac import require_permission
27	from app.core.schemas import Page
28	from app.modules.sales import service
29	from app.modules.sales.constants import (
30	    SALES_DELIVERY_MANAGE,
31	    SALES_DELIVERY_POST,
32	    SALES_DELIVERY_READ,
33	)
34	from app.modules.sales.schemas import (
35	    DeliveryCreate,
36	    DeliveryDetail,
37	    DeliveryLineRead,
38	    DeliveryRead,
39	)
40	
41	delivery_router = APIRouter(tags=["sales-deliveries"])
42	
43	CursorParamsDep = Depends(cursor_params)
44	_CreateIdem = Depends(Idempotent("sales.delivery.create"))
45	_PostIdem = Depends(Idempotent("sales.delivery.post"))
46	
47	
48	async def delivery_detail(
49	    session: SessionDep, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, delivery_id: uuid.UUID
50	) -> DeliveryDetail:
51	    delivery = await service.get_delivery(session, tenant_id, delivery_id)
52	    await session.refresh(delivery)
53	    lines = await service.get_delivery_lines(session, tenant_id, delivery_id)
54	    header = DeliveryRead.model_validate(delivery)
55	    return DeliveryDetail(
56	        **header.model_dump(),
57	        lines=[DeliveryLineRead.model_validate(line) for line in lines],
58	    )
59	
60	
61	@delivery_router.post(
62	    "/deliveries",
63	    response_model=DeliveryDetail,
64	    status_code=201,
65	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(SALES_DELIVERY_MANAGE))],
66	)
67	async def create_delivery(
68	    payload: DeliveryCreate,
69	    current: CurrentUserDep,
70	    session: SessionDep,
71	    idem: IdempotentDep = _CreateIdem,
72	) -> DeliveryDetail:
73	    """Create a DRAFT delivery against a sales order (PLAN 7.3): the order must be deliverable
74	    (CONFIRMED / PARTIALLY_DELIVERED), each line within the open-to-deliver quantity (over-delivery
75	    → 422), the source bin holds enough stock. IDEMPOTENT (D-013)."""
76	    holder: dict[str, DeliveryDetail] = {}
77	
78	    async def work() -> None:
79	        delivery = await service.create_delivery(session, current.tenant_id, payload)
80	        detail = await delivery_detail(session, current.tenant_id, delivery.id)
81	        holder["read"] = await idem.capture(detail, status_code=201)
82	
83	    await run_in_uow(session, work)
84	    return holder["read"]
85	
86	
87	@delivery_router.get(
88	    "/deliveries",
89	    response_model=Page[DeliveryRead],
90	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(SALES_DELIVERY_READ))],
91	)
92	async def list_deliveries(
93	    current: CurrentUserDep,
94	    session: SessionDep,
95	    params: CursorParams = CursorParamsDep,
96	    sales_order_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
97	    status: str | None = None,
98	) -> Page[DeliveryRead]:
99	    page = await service.list_deliveries(
100	        session,
101	        current.tenant_id,
102	        sales_order_id=sales_order_id,
103	        status=status,
104	        cursor=params.cursor,
105	        limit=params.limit,
106	    )
107	    return map_page(page, DeliveryRead)
108	
109	
110	@delivery_router.get(
111	    "/deliveries/{delivery_id}",
112	    response_model=DeliveryDetail,
113	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(SALES_DELIVERY_READ))],
114	)
115	async def get_delivery(
116	    delivery_id: uuid.UUID, current: CurrentUserDep, session: SessionDep
117	) -> DeliveryDetail:
118	    return await delivery_detail(session, current.tenant_id, delivery_id)
119	
120	
121	@delivery_router.post(
122	    "/deliveries/{delivery_id}/post",
123	    response_model=DeliveryDetail,
124	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(SALES_DELIVERY_POST))],
125	)
126	async def post_delivery(
127	    delivery_id: uuid.UUID,
128	    current: CurrentUserDep,
129	    session: SessionDep,
130	    idem: IdempotentDep = _PostIdem,
131	) -> DeliveryDetail:
132	    """Post a DRAFT delivery (PLAN 7.3, D-045): creates the stock ISSUE moves (Dr COGS / Cr
133	    Inventory via the event bus, COGS the default issue offset), raises the order line
134	    delivered_quantity, advances the order status — all one transaction. A closed delivery period or
135	    insufficient stock rolls the whole post back. IDEMPOTENT (D-013)."""
136	    holder: dict[str, DeliveryDetail] = {}
137	
138	    async def work() -> None:
139	        await service.post_delivery(session, current.tenant_id, delivery_id)
140	        detail = await delivery_detail(session, current.tenant_id, delivery_id)
141	        holder["read"] = await idem.capture(detail)
142	
143	    await run_in_uow(session, work)
144	    return holder["read"]
145	
146	
147	@delivery_router.post(
148	    "/deliveries/{delivery_id}/cancel",
149	    response_model=DeliveryDetail,
150	    dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(SALES_DELIVERY_MANAGE))],
151	)
152	async def cancel_delivery(
153	    delivery_id: uuid.UUID, current: CurrentUserDep, session: SessionDep
154	) -> DeliveryDetail:
155	    """Cancel a DRAFT delivery (PLAN 7.3). A POSTED delivery is terminal (corrected by a return /
156	    RMA, 7.4)."""
157	    holder: dict[str, DeliveryDetail] = {}
158	
159	    async def work() -> None:
160	        await service.cancel_delivery(session, current.tenant_id, delivery_id)
161	        holder["read"] = await delivery_detail(session, current.tenant_id, delivery_id)
162	
163	    await run_in_uow(session, work)
164	    return holder["read"]
